2. The facts that has given rise to this petition are : The respondent no. 1, Pubali Bank Ltd. instituted Title Suit No. 13 of 1993 in the aforesaid Court against the petitioner for recovery of the loan amount of Tk. 18,50,000/- as per account closed on June 11, 1990. After institution of the Suit the petitioner .filed written statement materially denying the averments made in the plaint and objecting to the amount for which decree sought for. The other pleadings are not necessary for disposal of this petition and accordingly we do not state those in this judgment. After filing written statement and additional written statement by the petitioner an application for examination of the account of the petitioner was filed by him through an appointed Commercial Audit. party of the Government and the Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal allowed the application.. The said application was filed under Order 26, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to such order the Accounts Commissioner appointed by the Court submitted a report on 10.11.93. The report was objected to by filing written objection by the plaintiff-bank. Thereafter, several dates were fixed for order relating to submission of the report and objection thereto. The Court fixed the suit for peremptory hearing on 18.8.94. But the petitioner filed 'an application for disposal of the objection raised by the plaintiff-bank against the report of the Commissioner, The Court fixed 27.9.94 for hearing objection and on hearing the parties the Court passed the order on that date to the following effect :- ‘‘প্রদিদ্বন্দ্বী উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবীর বক্তব্য শুনলাম। নিরীক্ষা সংক্রান্ত কমিশন প্রতিবেদন এবং আপত্তি নথীভুক্ত রাখা হউক। এতদসংক্রান্ত মূল মোকদ্দমার সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ গ্রহনকালে এবং তৎসহ প্রতিবেদন প্রদানকারী কমিশনারের সাক্ষ্য গ্রহনের মাধ্যমে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন পূর্বক মামলার বিচার নিষ্পত্তি হইবে। 

 5.  Mr. Hasan Ariff drawing our attention to the aforesaid provision of sub-Rule (2) of Rule 12 of Order 26 of the Code of Civil. Procedure contends. That if the evidence (report of the Accounts Cominissioner) is considered at the time of trial his cliant may be prejudiced if the report is not accepted which according to him states that the claim for decree in the suit by the plaintiff-bank is much less. He further submits that if at the time of trial the Court disbelieves the report them the decree will be made for higher amount and that will saddle the plaintiff for filing appeal under section 7(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 and that according to the aforesaid provision of the Act the appellant is to deposit 50% of the decretal amount to the trial Court for filing appeal against the decree. 

 6. True, that is so has enjoined by sub-section (2) of Section 7 of that Act. But the present petition is not out of a decree of Artha Rin Adalat, rather, it is from the order on the report submitted by the Accounts Commissioner. It lead us to examine another point as to whether the order which is being assailed before us is subject to appeal or amenable to writ jurisdiction or from such order a revision lies under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. Mr. Ariff seriously contends that as the order relates not to the decree made by the Court and as proviso to Section 7 (2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 speaks relating to interim order, the order impugned is amenable to the jurisdiction of this Court as conferred under Article 102 of our Constitution.
